decisions.reason: Eliminating the print-version deliverable does not change the requirement to arrange supplied materials into the magazine layout according to the current Flat Plan.
Image-quality remediation remains applicable to the digital magazine and is not stated to depend on production of a print version.
Advertisement sharpness was required for the supplied magazine PDF and remains relevant to the digital output independently of the removed print version.
The source removes only the print version; the digital flipbook remains the required deliverable unchanged.
The article-end whitespace requirement applies to the magazine layout and remains relevant to the digital flipbook after print output is removed.
The polished, brand-aligned visual style remains required for the digital magazine and is independent of the print deliverable.
Removing print output does not change the specified source of the magazine articles.
The cover-listed articles must still be included to keep the digital magazine consistent with its cover.
The approved readable Inter typography remains applicable to the digital magazine and is not limited to print output.
Future word-count guidance addresses layout whitespace in later issues and is not necessarily altered by removing the current print deliverable.
The red-usage policy concerns visual styling of the cover and an article, which remains applicable to the digital magazine.
Author names, photographs, sizing, sourcing, and placement remain required on digital article pages independently of print output.
